title: matter: Properly dissect Additional Data characteristic
description:
The dissector is based on Matter Specification Version 1.3, section
5.4.2.5.7 GATT-based Additional Data.

Additional changes:
- added payload length information to the listing info column for easier
  packets inspection

I've removed this check. Now, the `dissect_matter_chr_ad_tlv()` calls `matter.tlv` dissector which properly dissects Matter-defined TLV containers. So, even if the top-level TLV container is not a structure, the data should be dissected properly. This will allow to dissect payloads which do not follow the spec, which might help debugging communication issues.
Please avoid using ws_warning() in dissectors. Presumably you want to use an expert info instead.

I like the approach of generalizing the TLV parsing for future use, but any reason why it is not included in packet-matter.c instead of creating a new packet-matter-common.c file?

That would not be the first time a single source file registers more than one dissector. And it could be associate to the Matter protocol rather than a (what seems to be) fake Matter TLV protocol.

What do you think?

> any reason why it is not included in packet-matter.c

No, there is no any particular reason. The last time when I've added another dissector to already existing one, some CI check failed. So, I thought that the way to go is to keep one dissector in one file. But, if actually the right way is to group dissectors based on function, I'll merge this fake TLV protocol into matter. And, yes, it might be used within the matter as well (that's why it's generalized now).
I've integrated Matter-TLV into Matter protocol.
